status_summary: As of 2026-10-07 no executive order reshaping the USGCRP was found in a Federal Register search of presidential documents. The administration instead acted through OSTP and personnel decisions. Work on the Sixth National Climate Assessment (NCA6) was halted and its authors dismissed in April 2025, and the assessment website went offline on 2025-06-30. In 2026 the program was reconstituted: Eos and E&E News reported on 2026-07-09 that Matthew Wielicki, whom E&E News describes as a climate critic and Eos as a climate skeptic, heads the USGCRP and the assessment, and a Federal Register notice of 2026-08-25 lists him as USGCRP Director at OSTP; Eos also reports that researchers known for climate skepticism were brought in during December 2025. That notice, issued by OSTP on behalf of the USGCRP, sought comment until 2026-09-09 on a proposed amendment to the 2023 Fifth National Climate Assessment (NCA5) under which results that depend materially on high-emissions scenarios would not be presented as expected or baseline planning futures unless reproduced under a presently plausible scenario; the rest of NCA5 would be kept. This tracks the Mandate's call to critically review a Biden-era assessment, by agency action rather than the order it recommends, and the amendment is proposed, not final.

timeline.event: Per a Wikipedia summary of NPR reporting, work on the Sixth National Climate Assessment is halted when its funding and contractor support end.
Per a Wikipedia summary citing the New York Times, all authors and contributors working on the Sixth National Climate Assessment are dismissed and the scope is said to be under re-evaluation.

The website hosting the most recent National Climate Assessment stops working; NASA says on 2025-07-01 that all five editions will be posted on its own website, date to be set, and the White House did not respond on plans for a next edition.

Eos reports that in December 2025 the administration brought in researchers known for climate skepticism to restart work on the Sixth National Climate Assessment (month known only; first of month used).

Eos and E&E News report that Matthew Wielicki, a former University of Alabama geochemist, heads the reconstituted USGCRP and the National Climate Assessment; Eos says he asked the public on 2026-06-29 what NCA6 should include and that a White House spokesperson welcomed the appointment. Neither article gives the appointing authority or an exact appointment date.

OSTP, on behalf of the USGCRP, publishes a Federal Register notice (91 FR 54893, signed 2026-08-20) seeking comment on a proposed amendment and clarification to NCA5: results that depend materially on high-emissions scenarios such as RCP8.5 and SSP5-8.5 should not be presented as expected, baseline or ordinary planning futures unless reproduced under a presently plausible scenario, though they may serve as disclosed sensitivity or stress tests; the rest of NCA5 is kept. The notice lists Matthew Wielicki as USGCRP Director at OSTP. EDGI describes the proposal as calling the worst case implausible.
Comment period on the proposed NCA5 amendment closes at 11:59 p.m. Eastern (docket metadata lists 2026-09-10); no final decision was found as of 2026-10-07.

title: Reshape the US Global Change Research Program and its climate assessments
uncertainties: The appointing authority and exact date of Wielicki's role are not stated in the articles read (E&E News cites his social media and an anonymous source; Eos cites Politico, which was not read). The word 'implausible' for the worst-case scenario comes from EDGI, an advocacy-leaning research group; the Federal Register notice does not give the amended text. The April 2025 halt and dismissals rest on Wikipedia summaries and the NPR piece. Whether NASA ever posted the five prior assessments was not confirmed (globalchange.gov returned only an old snapshot). The July 2025 Energy Department climate report was not examined. A Federal Register search of presidential documents for 'Global Change Research' returned only a 2026-01-16 withdrawal-from-organizations document, with no order on the USGCRP.
